name: NetBox Docker
what_it_is: A community-maintained Docker/Compose packaging of NetBox, a network source-of-truth application providing IP address management (IPAM) and data-center infrastructure management (DCIM). It orchestrates the NetBox web application, background worker, PostgreSQL database, and two Valkey (Redis-compatible) cache instances.
components: netbox — Django/Gunicorn application server serving the web UI and REST/GraphQL APIs on port 8080
netbox-worker — RQ background task processor for async jobs (webhooks, scripts, reports)
postgres — PostgreSQL 18 relational database storing all NetBox data
redis — Valkey 9.0 instance used as the primary message broker and job queue
redis-cache — Valkey 9.0 instance used as the application object cache (separate from the queue)
protocols: HTTP REST API — full CRUD over /api/ endpoints for all NetBox objects
GraphQL — available at /graphql/ for flexible query-based data retrieval
HTTP — web UI served on container port 8080 (no TLS termination in compose; handled externally)
measurement: No built-in metrics exporter in the compose stack; NetBox exposes no Prometheus endpoint by default
Health state is checked via HTTP GET on the NetBox container every 15 s after a 90 s startup window
Worker liveness is verified by checking the RQWorker process every 15 s after a 20 s startup window
Database readiness is polled with pg_isready every 10 s
Redis/Valkey liveness is confirmed via PING every 1 s
configuration: Runtime settings injected via env files: env/netbox.env, env/postgres.env, env/redis.env, env/redis-cache.env
docker-compose.override.yml pattern used for local customisation without modifying the base file
SUPERUSER_* environment variables enable automated admin account creation on first run
TLS termination must be configured externally (reverse proxy); the compose stack does not expose TLS
LDAP integration available via additional configuration in netbox.env / custom plugin settings
Image version pinned via VERSION build-arg (default v4.5-4.0.2); must match the Git tag checked out
fault_injection: No native fault-injection tooling included; network partitions between services can be simulated by removing the shared Docker network or stopping individual containers
Stopping the redis container while netbox is running triggers job-queue failures observable in the worker logs
Stopping postgres simulates a database-unavailable scenario; NetBox returns 500 errors on data operations
modes: release — tracks the latest stable vX.Y.Z tag, rebuilt ~every 24 h
latest — production-ready builds from the most recent release branch
snapshot — pre-release builds from the main development branch; may be unstable
constraints: Docker >= 20.10.10 and containerd >= 1.5.6 are required; older Docker versions are unsupported
docker-compose >= 1.28.0 is required for the override-file merge behaviour to work correctly
The container image version tag must match the Git repository tag checked out; mismatches cause migration errors
No port is published to the host in the default compose file — a separate reverse proxy or override is required for external access
The stack uses six named volumes; data is not portable without explicit volume backup/restore procedures
Kubernetes deployments are documented separately and are not covered by the base compose configuration
notable_absences: No Prometheus/metrics sidecar or exporter in the default stack
No TLS termination — HTTPS requires an external reverse proxy (nginx, Traefik, etc.)
No netbox-housekeeping service in the compose file (must be added manually for scheduled cleanup tasks)
No log aggregation or structured log shipping configured
No seed/fixture data loader — the database starts empty and requires manual bootstrapping or API imports
